items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: Oh we do this song with Dave Matthews, who became a big friend of the band’s.

ctx.x: Have you ever been tempted to do more vocal work?

I’m not opposed to it. We tried it for a while and it was because I wrote a bunch of songs and that was one of the things that triggered that whole conversation again for the first time in a long time, it’s oh we’ve got Dave Matthews on your record and you’re singing this stuff and like are you trying to make pop records? What are you guys trying to do? This isn’t why we buy Flecktone records is to hear this stuff. And I remember there was a song we had called “Communication,” which at the time I wrote it about a…

we weren’t communicating very well in the band. It was a very simple thing. Communication is the only way to start saying what you mean to say. It’s the kind of thing if Sting sang people would say, “oh what a great simple lyric.” But because it was my first song on a record people said “wow, what an idiotic lyric.”
